Let the noon find thee by other lakes, and the night overtake thee everywhere at home.
There are no larger fields than these, no worthier games than may here be played. Grow wild according
to thy nature, like these sedges and breaks which will never become English hay. Let the
thunder rumble. What if it threaten ruin to farmers' crops? That is not its errand to thee.
Take shelter under the cloud while they flee to carts and sheds. Let not to get a living
be thy trade, but thy sport. Enjoy the land, but own it not. Through one of enterprise and
